name: A forbidden marriage
about: The children of two houses that hate each other fall in love. A parent forbids it, and they either obey, run off or get hunted down, and whichever house is stronger decides who keeps them.
title: The Forbidden Match of {a.houseName} and {b.houseName}
fade: {a} and {b} stop writing. Whatever it was, {thread} is just a song now, and people sing it wrong.

beats.speaker: a
text: At the harvest fair in {elder.seat}, {a} of {a.house} and {b} of {b.house} dance three dances together, and people notice.
{a} and {b} meet at a hawking party neither house should have gone to, and ride back far behind the others.

memory.a: I danced with {b} of {b.house}. I think of nothing else.
memory.b: I met {a} of {a.house}, whose house my {b.father} hates. I don't care.

beats.speaker: b
beats.text: Letters pass between {a} and {b}, hidden in loaves and saddlebags. A maid of {elder.house} reads one, and tells.

memory.elder: My {a.son} {a} has been writing to {b}, the {b.son} of {rival}.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {a} kneels before {elder} and asks to marry {b} of {rival.house}. {elder} says {elder.he} will think about it, and sends a rider to {rival}.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: Bells ring in {elder.seat}: {a} marries {b}, and {elder.house} and {rival.house} drink from one cup. The old grudges are buried, for now.

memory.elder: I let my {a.son} marry into {rival.house}. I hope it ends the old quarrel.
memory.rival: My {b.son} {b} married {a} of {elder.house}. {elder} and I are family now.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} forbids it: no child of {elder.house} will marry into {rival.house}. {a} is locked in a tower room at {elder.seat}.

memory.a: {elder} forbade me {b} and locked me in a tower like a thief.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {a} does what {elder} says. {b} is promised to someone else within the year, and {a} stays away from the wedding feast.

memory.a: I gave up {b} because {elder} commanded it. I will not forgive it.
memory.b: {a} would not stand up to {a.his} {elder.father} for me.

a.text: make {elder} answer for what was taken from me

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {a} slips out of {elder.seat} by the side gate and rides to {b}. A hedge priest marries them at dawn, with a ploughman as witness.

memory.a: I married {b} before a hedge priest at dawn. Let them come.
memory.b: {a} came to me through the night. We are married.
memory.elder: My {a.son} ran off to marry into {rival.house}. It was theft, and {rival} is the thief.
memory.rival: My {b.son} married {a} of {elder.house} without my leave.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} calls the marriage theft and rides on {rival.seat} with swords to take {a} back.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {elder}'s riders drag {a} back to {elder.seat}. The priests undo the marriage, and {b} is left bleeding by the road.

memory.a: My {elder.father}'s men dragged me home and the priests undid my marriage to {b}.
memory.b: {elder}'s riders took {a} from me on the road and left me in the ditch.

die.how: I died on the road trying to keep {a}.

beats.speaker: b
beats.text: {elder}'s army turns for home. {a} and {b} keep their home under {rival.house}'s banners, and a child is born before the snow.

memory.a: My {elder.father} could not take me back. My home is with {b} now.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} rages for a week, then sends a cask of wine after the couple. What's done is done.
{a} and {b} die before the houses can part them. The bells ring in {elder.seat} and {rival.seat} alike, and each house blames the other.
